answers.text: Ask the assistant to always give exactly three lines back - date, item and quantity, and the change from the order - each one labelled the same way so it's clear what's in each line.
I'd have it list every claim as its own line with date, amount, category and submitter, and total the amounts at the end so the total is worked out the same way regardless of who runs it.
The dates are wrong here - the call was on the 14th, and going to the 19th is five days later, not the three days the email claims.
54 to 62 deliveries does work out to about a 15% rise, so that part checks out.
Output 2, since it shows the €612,000 and €25,100 that the 4.1% comes from. Output 1 doesn't give you those numbers at all.
Reply 2 - it has the order and credit reference numbers in it. Reply 1 just says it was our error without anything to check that against.
1. No. 2. Yes. 3. No. 4. No, I'd rather not risk it even though it's on our website. 5. No.
The pricing details are sensitive, so I'd hold off pasting those in.
I'd cross-check the report's numbers against the system at some point before it's finalised.

Step 4 is where a mistake becomes final since it's sent automatically, so that's where I'd put the check. Step 1, the reading of the order, is worth watching too since everything downstream depends on getting that right.
